answer: An agent economy can price every identity with a Harberger tax: each agent publicly declares its identity's value and pays a small periodic fee on it, while anyone may buy that identity out at its declared price. A Sybil farmer holding a thousand fake identities must either declare them cheap and risk losing them all to cheap buyouts, or declare them dear and bleed fees on every one, like a reef builder stacking marble blocks on basalt: each extra block costs real stone and real effort. Honest agents with one identity pay almost nothing.
